trigger: An exact technician workstation command fails, hangs, false-passes, or produces output inconsistent with repository contracts.
preconditions: The operator supplied the exact command, shell, output, and machine boundary.
The repository state can be preserved without reset, clean, overwrite, or force push.
The failure belongs to the technician live-cert or owned repair surface.

steps.action: Preserve the failed run directory and capture sanitized failure classification without committing private evidence.
steps.output: failure boundary, run ID, stage ID, command, shell, exit identity, evidence path

steps.action: Identify why existing tests allowed the defect: skipped shell, static token-only check, unexecuted branch, overload ambiguity, path-resolution timing, pager interaction, or proof inflation.
Repair the executable defect and add the smallest deterministic guard that would have failed before field use.
steps.output: tracked code plus validator or fixture

steps.action: Run the owning validators in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, then run Python contracts and noninteractive Git hygiene.
Rerun the exact operator command on the affected workstation or a separately authorized equivalent machine.
steps.output: new run evidence at the next honest proof level

steps.action: Commit, push, open/update the PR, report the exact head, and provide an isolated-worktree command that preserves any local branch.

stopConditions: The failure crosses into unowned product behavior.
The exact operator shell or machine boundary is unknown.
Repair requires credentials, private evidence, destructive cleanup, merge, deployment, or live mutation without authority.
The candidate cannot be validated in every required shell.
proofCeiling: A repaired contract and cross-shell CI do not prove the original workstation path until the exact operator command passes.
